tasks.title: Trial: railway run with real rails in a study area (owner picks the stretch)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and the stretch, and says whether it may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 5 and 6. Owner idea 2026-11-10: real Minecraft rails for long runs of railway, with land height and direction hacking. This is a spike: the deliverable is findings plus a throwaway prototype, not a production builder. Stretch: at least 300 blocks with a curve and a cutting or embankment. Steps: (1) get the railway lines for the area (railway is not in CELL_EXTRACT_LAYERS today; state where they come from, for example a one-off extract from the world's OSM provider) and snap the centreline to a rail-legal path (long cardinal runs, 90-degree corners, diagonals as staircases); (2) take a lidar ground profile along it, smooth and clamp to a gentle gradient (find the real-world figure from a source and cite it), level the corridor with cut or fill and grass side slopes; (3) lay ballast and rails, with one ascending rail only where a step is needed; (4) apply under the site lock with a structure backup and look in game with the owner. First version leaves out bridges, tunnels, road crossings, fences, stations and signals; note where each would be needed. The prototype lives in the scratchpad, or on a task/* branch only if the owner wants to keep it. Game rules to confirm on the current client: rail needs a solid block below, slopes only on straight cardinal runs at 1 block per block, curves flat, diagonals as staircases. Deliver findings in docs/plans/railway.md: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the corridor, minutes and session tokens used (method stated), and a recommendation with the follow-up implementation tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and any snags go to the named world's repo; standing up a new world is separate world work. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the run reads as a railway and the corridor looks natural is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: rule-built typology buildings versus per-building specs (owner picks terrace, estate and shop parade)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and three study streets, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 2 and 6. Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. This is a spike. The prototype generates minimal specs for the existing builders (house_build and feature_build); it does not add a third builder. Baseline is house_build with a minimal spec versus a full feature_build spec for the same buildings. Study streets: a terrace, a semi-detached or detached estate street, a shop parade. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Woodland: dense fill, mixed species, understorey and woodland floor
tasks.notes: Deliverable: inside wood polygons, fill towards the aerial canopy cover (about 80%), mixed species and heights, understorey bushes (persistent leaves at Y+1 to Y+2) and ferns, podzol/coarse_dirt/moss_block floor with grass at the edges; labelled inference, removable through the foliage and decor masks. Owner: trees need more density. Performance evidence clarified 2026-11-21 (read-only): the trial quotes 962 s for 113 trees, but 8.5 s per tree is only an average of the reported total, not a measured per-tree bottleneck. The saved farmland trees-result.json (journal_seq 1292) records 17,915 positions, writer total 2.35 s, and 40.38 s summed across recorded apply stages; planning before site_kit.apply is not included in that result. The code already batches tree writes into one cell plan. The cause of the remainder of the reported command time is not established; profile planning and full command stages before choosing an optimisation or projecting dense-woodland cost. The earlier live-planning cache-thrash/low-probe-floor problem has a landed fix in #315 (planning from saved regions); distinguish it from the still-unexplained 962 s total. Numeric runtime limit remains to be agreed. Check: wood across the river in cell 63,-45 matches the aerial density; apply time for it stays under a stated limit; owner verdict in game. Profile 2026-11-21 (read-only dry run of trees_layer on 87,-48 under cProfile, current code with #315): 85 s total. planning_inputs 52.9 s, of which neighbour_owned 36 s (cell_journal._cell_owners rebuilds ownership per cell, uncacheable because builds are excluded; about 9 million block_id calls; scales with journal history, not tree count); dry site_kit.apply 16.9 s; surface warm-up 5.6 s; plan_cell (tree placement) 5.7 s. Dry run planted 51 trees and 10,306 blocks, not the trial's 113 trees and 17,915 positions, so it is indicative only. Current planning is about a minute, so the 962 s is not explained by planning on current code: it was pre-#315 live planning or the live apply stages (MCP write and readback), which a dry run cannot show. Next: time a live apply with the existing timed_stage output; the ownership lookup is a candidate optimisation. Live apply 2026-11-21 (87,-48, after prepare --apply cleared a stale readiness validation): 77 s wall, but NOT a clean redo and NOT the 113-tree workload. The apply did not undo the earlier trees pass (the dry run simulates that undo, apply_cell does not), so 51 crowns were skipped as trunk blocked and only 3 trees (556 blocks) were planted on top. Stages: layer planning 38.6 s, identity and readiness 4.1 s, journal begin 6.1 s, writer total 12.7 s (player hop 9.3 s), flush 3.6 s, readback 0.4 s. Side effect, owner chose not to repair: the trees mask for 87,-48 now holds 556 positions instead of the 17,915 of journal #1292, so the original trees remain in the world but are outside the mask (mask-based undo or redo would only touch the 3 new trees). A real full-workload timing needs undo then apply of the trees pass, on a cell where that is acceptable. Ghost frontier finding 2026-11-21 (ground apply on 46,-46, run from prepare then ground): the apply took 984 s and 883 s of it was the 'journal follow-ups' stage (registry.ensure writing 7 frontier ghost cells, journal #1656-1668, about 126 s and 1.1 million planned blocks per cell); every other stage summed to about 100 s. Owner decision: the ghost frontier is wanted and stays; it must be completed before a timing starts, so measure applies on cells whose frontier already exists (the follow-ups stage then takes about 0 s, as on 87,-48). This does not explain the trial's 962 s: the 87,-48 trees apply (#1292) had no ghost builds after it. Still open: a full-workload trees timing needs an open-land cell with no planned features and a valid readiness check; 46,-46 is blocked by the planned houses_burgess_road feature (must land before trees/decor) and a stale validation (#232). Full-workload trees timing 2026-11-21 (46,-46 after the houses landed and a ground redo, frontier already complete so journal follow-ups took 0.003 s; existing planner, 256 crowns, 41,160 blocks, readback 0 mismatches): about 100 s of stage time. layer planning 54.2 s; registry.begin guard reads and journal write 14.0 s; surface warm-up in apply 9.8 s; readback 8.6 s; identity and readiness 3.9 s; flush 3.3 s; writer 2.6 s; backup 1.0 s. Placement is not the cost, and the trial 962 s is still unexplained (likely before #315 and #343, or a pending frontier). A runtime limit of a few minutes looks reachable; the numeric limit is still to be agreed. Dry-run cProfile of planning (inflated by the profiler): _box about 24 s, aerial tile decoding about 14 s, lidar about 7 s, neighbour_owned about 6.6 s, plan_cell about 6 s. Filed #345 for the box filter and decode caching; not filed: profiling registry.begin and the apply warm-up, and timing ground and decor. The earlier open blockers (planned house feature, stale validation) are cleared on 46,-46. Owner feedback on the existing planner, filed as issue I-055 (held until #318): too sparse versus the aerial (dense wood with a few clearings), grass floor where podzol and ground cover belong, and no species variety. Runtime limit agreed 2026-11-21: 8 minutes for a tree build; flag at 8, kill at 12 (150%), continue to the next cell in long runs, and report every 8+ minute tree build at the end of the run. The watchdog and reporting are filed as a separate task (see the task list entry Run budget for long runs). What #318 still needs: the woodland design work (diagnose why the existing cover-based fill is still sparse; species mix; understorey; podzol/moss/fern floor) and the 63,-45 check. Proving cells agreed 2026-11-21: both 63,-45 (the wood across the river; validation stale, needs prepare --apply) and 46,-46 (small wood beside the Burgess Road houses; existing planner already applied, owner snags I-055 filed against it). The check is the woodland density matching the aerial, the apply under the 8 minute budget, and the owner verdict in game, on both. Sparse-fill diagnosis 2026-11-21 (read-only, 46,-46, existing planner dry run; lidar nDSM vs planted crown discs): cover_pixels detector calls 62% of the cell cover (>=0.6), 30% firm (>=0.9), mean 0.63; lidar says only 37% of columns are 3 m or taller (43% at 2 m); planted crowns shade 47% of the cell. Only 48% of lidar-tall (>=3 m) columns have a crown (50% at >=8 m). Of the tall columns left without a crown, 59% have aerial cover under COVER_MIN 0.6 so fill_dense never considers them (owner hypothesis: obscured crowns in dense wood are missed and become gaps; supported), 25% sit at cover 0.6-0.9 and 16% at >=0.9 (thinned by the probability ramp or the FILL_SPACING 5 grid). Crowns also shade about 29% of the cell where lidar is under 3 m, so the planner both misses tall columns and plants over low ground. Only 23 crowns are lidar-detected; about 295 candidates come from the fill, 62 of 318 skipped (34 trunk blocked). Lidar alone does not give the owner density (tall columns 37% vs 47% already shaded); aerial and lidar may differ in date or in what counts as tall, so 63,-45 is the cleaner check. Proposal, not yet decided: use lidar-tall columns left bare as a second crown source and keep aerial cover only for what lidar cannot see; this is layer-changing planner work (a stretch: ask before raising model or effort). After #345 (merged f136d5e): dry run on 46,-46 still plants 256 crowns and 41,160 blocks. planning_inputs wall time 26.9 s (the earlier live layer-planning stage was 54.2 s, which also included surface warm-up). RE-SCOPED 2026-11-21: the mechanisms are split into fixture-only tasks that any runner can take: plant vocabulary (#347), woodland floor in the ground layer (#348, blocked by #347), lidar-tall second crown source (#349), species mix (#350), understorey bushes (#351); speed (#345) and run budget (#346) are separate. Layer ownership (owner, corrected 2026-11-21): ground sets the ground level at lidar terrain height (the podzol, coarse dirt and moss floor blocks, #348); trees do only trees (#349 lidar crowns, #350 species); decor does the minor non-feature, non-tree enhancements, i.e. understorey bushes, ferns, leaf litter and other plants (#351). The rough-grass trial (trial259_roughgrass_87_m48) is the source of the floor palette. #318 now keeps what needs Claude: choosing thresholds, shares and species weights against the aerial, a ground redo then trees redo on both proving cells (63,-45 and 46,-46), the 8 minute check, and the owner verdict in game. It is blocked by #348-#351. #349 and #350 both edit trees_layer.py: run them one at a time. #348 edits ground_layer.py and #351 decor_layer.py. Open for the owner: #319's rough-grass tufts and flowers are placed by the ground layer, which the ownership rule above would put in decor.

tasks.title: Review: rationalise half-shared modules and parallel seams (started by roof materials)
tasks.notes:
Owner prompt 2026-11-21 after #355: a shared roof-material catalogue landed that only feature_build uses, while house_build still invents `{mat}_slab`, and terrace.py / outbuildings.py keep their own ROOF_FULL tables. That is bad code: a "shared" seam with one caller, deferred "Task 2" still open, and parallel material maps elsewhere. Feel bad; do not paper over it.

Deliverable: a short review of the tool codebase and the open system tracker (tasks/index.json, not world ISSUES), then proposed new tasks that rationalise duplicated or half-shared seams. Write findings under docs/plans/ (one file). The review itself does not change production code; the follow-up tickets do.

Prompting example (must address): roof materials. Catalogue + roof_material.py + feature_build wrapper versus house_build string slabs versus terrace ROOF_FULL versus outbuildings ROOF_FULL. Propose either wire every builder through one module, or delete the pretence of sharing and keep one call site.

Also scan for the same pattern elsewhere: modules or configs that claim to be shared but have one caller; thin wrappers that only relocate names; deferred "phase 2" notes that left the first merge as bloat; parallel tables for the same vocabulary (block families, plant names, land-use keys, builder registration).

Open tasks: read every active ticket's title and notes. Flag tickets that add more parallel seams, that depend on unfinished sharing, or that should be rewritten or blocked until a rationalisation task lands. Do not close tickets in this pass unless the owner agrees; propose closes or rewrites in the plan.

Out of scope: live world builds, cell registry work, rewriting #355 in place without a filed follow-up. requiresClaude false: source and tracker reading only.

Check: plan file exists with (1) concrete bad seams found, (2) open-task interactions, (3) proposed new task titles and one-paragraph scopes ready to add. Owner reviews before any of those are filed.

tasks.notes:
Owner I-057 S-104: the designer should pick roof material from colour and pattern, with recommended triads for common roofs (red tile, grey tile and the like); cut copper was the owner's example for the Burgess Road houses and must not be hard-coded.
Deliverable: named roof types added to the the shared roof-material module (#355, merged: lib/builds/roof_material.py, config/roof-materials.json) catalogue (red clay tile, grey slate or tile, brown or weathered tile, weathered copper, flat deck; thatch has no vanilla triad so it is flatish-only or left out), each with a recommended pitched triad (or flatish block for flat decks) and one or two alternates, generic and UK-wide, chosen by comparing the vanilla families' colour and texture with real roof colours read from the aerial for the existing specs (houses_burgess_road, w149814013 and a few others; read-only evidence from the world checkout, nothing from it stored in the tracker or the tool repo, using roof_zone_colour_lines and site_kit.nearest_preview_colour) and a look at each triad in game on a test roof (block_render_region or an in-game build). A lookup by type returns the triad; the designer brief lines in rules/feature-builds.md and rules/terrace-builds.md name the types.
Files: the the shared roof-material module (#355, merged: lib/builds/roof_material.py, config/roof-materials.json) catalogue file and module (types section), the two rules files, test for type resolution.
Check: (1) test: every named type resolves to catalogue families and every pitched type's family is a triad. (2) A short table in the task closing note: type, chosen family, aerial colour sample, in-game picture path. (3) Owner review step: I-057 S-104 after the next house design picks its roof by type.
Covers: I-057 (S-104). Not covered: respecc'ing existing specs (Burgess Road respec follows Tasks 1b and 2).

tasks.title: House roofs use the shared roof rule: pitched roofs get stairs, flat(ish) keep slabs (I-056 S-103)
tasks.notes:
Cause (I-056, read from code): House.roof in lib/builds/house_build.py (~384-437) sets y = b+6+d//2 by Chebyshev ring distance d, places only {mat}_slab (bottom even d, top odd), fills b+6..y-1 with WALL (bricks, line 37). Rise per ring is half a block, exactly 1 in 2, which by the shared rule is flat(ish) (the boundary), so the old roof never needs stairs. There is no pitched mode: stair() (line 47, no shape argument) is unused for roofs. The Burgess Road roofs are probably steeper hipped clay tile (spec notes; aerial and lidar slope not verified). Owner snag S-103.
Deliverable: pitch enters the spec as a new key `roof_pitch {label: rise_per_run}` parallel to `roofs` (the `roofs` values stay plain strings, which load_spec checks); absent means flatish, so existing specs build exactly as today. house_build takes roof_class from the the shared roof-material module (#355, merged: roof_class, roof_blocks, validate_roof_material in lib/builds/roof_material.py) module. Flatish: today's slab rings. Pitched: one roof-material stair per ring facing its higher neighbour (as terrace.py does), outer/inner corner shapes written explicitly via lib/audit/roof_lint.stair_shape_from_neighbours (house stair() gains a shape argument), a slab or opposed-stair cap where rings meet, chimney and ridge height recomputed (they read the `done` dict), support fill under each column a solid block so no wrong colour shows through a stair's open half, group mode (one roof over several houses) handled. Names come from the the shared roof-material module (#355, merged: roof_class, roof_blocks, validate_roof_material in lib/builds/roof_material.py) module. load_spec validates each roof material with validate_roof_material (warning); the module docstring (line 11) documents roof_pitch.
Files: lib/builds/house_build.py; lib/builds/test_house_build.py (ChimneyTest roof test ~224-253 asserts brick_slab and is kept for flatish, with pitched tests added); rules/terrace-builds.md roofs lines.
Check: (1) red-first fixture tests on square, L-shaped and group footprints: flatish equals the old slab roof; pitched has every slope stair facing its higher neighbour with explicit corner shapes and no slab-only slope. (2) Dry run of houses_burgess_road with roof_pitch set and a catalogue triad: stair/slab/block counts printed; `python3 scripts/roof_lint.py` and guard_roof_jogs clean. (3) Owner review step after Burgess Road is respecced to pitched and rebuilt: I-056 S-103 ("house roofs use stairs and slabs, not whole blocks"). I-056 stays open until then.
Covers: I-056 (S-103). Not covered: picking the material and pitch for Burgess Road (a respec after both tasks land); feature_build roofs (I-019).
Related: #356 (review of half-shared seams) names house_build's own {mat}_slab as the example; this task is the concrete house_build wiring, so #356 should treat it as already ticketed and not duplicate it. terrace.py and outbuildings.py ROOF_FULL stay out of scope here.

tasks.title: Roof PV from aerial: shared palette, dark arrays, CLI hardening
tasks.notes:
Follow-ups from #337 (big-box roof follows the aerial, merged in fa3826d; findings in docs/plans/bigbox-roof-aerial.md):
1. The roof_aerial palette should come from the shared roof-material catalogue (#355, config/roof-materials.json). 5 of its 9 materials are missing there: polished_andesite, polished_diorite, smooth_quartz, polished_deepslate, smooth_sandstone.
2. PV detection needs blue minus red of at least 30, so black-cell or dark-grey UK arrays are never found. Expose blue_margin and min_cells on the CLI, or detect dark arrays too.
3. The 0.4 m/px resolution gate (ppb < 2.5) can refuse exactly 0.4 m/px through float noise. Compare with an epsilon and test the boundary.
4. Arrays at an angle to the block grid are laid as their rectangular outline. Arrays clipped at a cell edge (the western ends of Westquay's NW and SW arrays, in 42,-16) are dropped.
5. Small CLI points:
   - --replace-pv without --write does nothing silently;
   - the mosaic name cross-check is skipped silently when the name has no zNN-WxH-TX-TY pattern;
   - main() has no docstring;
   - main, _footprint, _mosaic_affine and review_sheet have no tests.
6. feature_build PvArraysTest gaps: a box spanning two roof levels (commonest-deck filter), zone_materials, a top block that is not roof material, and a no-pv_arrays build equal to the old output. Also fix the stale "cell above is still free" wording in the pv_rows docstring.
